problem_type: Three-dimensional container loading combinatorial optimization with per-unit-area load-bearing limits, involving discrete selection, discrete orientations, and continuous coordinates. The sole objective is to maximize volume utilization: sum_{i=0..N-1} sum_{k=0..box_quantities[i]-1} s[i][k]×box_lengths[i]×box_widths[i]×box_heights[i], divided by container_length×container_width×container_height; it must not be changed to maximizing the number or weight of boxes, there is no secondary objective, and all feasible solutions tied at the maximum utilization are optimal. All quantity, orientation, boundary, full single-box support, non-overlap, and cumulative load-bearing limits are hard constraints, using exact equalities and non-strict inequalities with no relaxation tolerance. The complete solution dictionary contains five decision fields s, x, y, z, o; occupied dimensions, support relations, cumulative loads, and utilization are all derived from the input and these five fields and are not additional decision variables. Each example below uniformly uses N=2, box_quantities=[2,0] to show the array structure; they only illustrate structure, and feasibility still depends on the specific dimension, orientation-permission, and load-bearing inputs.

decisions.business: Whether candidate box k of box type i is loaded: 1 means loaded, 0 means not loaded. Selection is only from the given candidate boxes; using up each type's quantity limit is not required.
decisions.shape: list[list[int]]; outer length exactly N, row i has length exactly box_quantities[i], a 2D array with variable row lengths; the first array axis is box type i and the second is candidate box k of that type, both 0-based; elements are only the integers 0 or 1, booleans not accepted. [] when N=0; a row must be [] when that type's quantity limit is 0.
decisions.completeness: Every candidate box must have an entry; do not list only the loaded boxes, and do not omit rows or items, use null, or add candidate boxes. For each type, the sum of all s[i][k] must not exceed box_quantities[i]. Partial loading is allowed, as is all 0; when N=0 or all stock is 0, all five solution fields must still be submitted, with shapes determined by the input; the empty sum is 0 and the volume utilization is 0. The same [i][k] in all five fields must always refer to the same candidate box.

decisions.business: Coordinate of the front-bottom-left corner of candidate box k of box type i along the container length direction (spatial x-axis), in U_l, the same unit as all input edge lengths.
decisions.shape: list[list[float]], elements are JSON numbers, integer or decimal allowed; outer length exactly N, row i has length exactly box_quantities[i]; the first array axis is box type i and the second is candidate box k, both 0-based. All elements must be finite non-negative reals; coordinates are continuous and need not be integers; [] when N=0, and rows for zero-quantity box types must be [].
decisions.completeness: Must contain the coordinates of all candidate boxes; do not omit unloaded boxes or use null. The x of an unloaded box may be any finite non-negative real, is not forced to 0, and is not subject to container boundary or geometric checks. For a loaded box, x+dx <= container_length. Any two loaded boxes b, c must also satisfy at least one of the following six: x_b+dx_b <= x_c; x_c+dx_c <= x_b; y_b+dy_b <= y_c; y_c+dy_c <= y_b; z_b+dz_b <= z_c; z_c+dz_c <= z_b. That is, no volumetric overlap; face, edge, and point contact are allowed; each occupied dimension must be derived via the fixed mapping from o.

decisions.business: Coordinate of the front-bottom-left corner of candidate box k of box type i along the container width direction (spatial y-axis), in U_l, the same unit as all input edge lengths.
decisions.shape: list[list[float]], elements are JSON numbers, integer or decimal allowed; outer length exactly N, row i has length exactly box_quantities[i]; the first array axis is box type i and the second is candidate box k, both 0-based. All elements must be finite non-negative reals; coordinates are continuous and need not be integers; [] when N=0, and rows for zero-quantity box types must be [].
decisions.completeness: Must contain the coordinates of all candidate boxes; do not omit unloaded boxes or use null. The y of an unloaded box may be any finite non-negative real, is not forced to 0, and is not subject to container boundary or geometric checks. For a loaded box, y+dy <= container_width; together with x, z, o it must also satisfy the non-overlap and full-support conditions.

decisions.business: Height of the front-bottom-left corner of candidate box k of box type i, along the vertically upward spatial z-axis, in U_l, the same unit as all input edge lengths; z=0 means the bottom face is on the floor.
decisions.shape: list[list[float]], elements are JSON numbers, integer or decimal allowed; outer length exactly N, row i has length exactly box_quantities[i]; the first array axis is box type i and the second is candidate box k, both 0-based. All elements must be finite non-negative reals; coordinates are continuous and need not be integers; [] when N=0, and rows for zero-quantity box types must be [].
decisions.completeness: Must contain the coordinates of all candidate boxes; do not omit unloaded boxes or use null. The z of an unloaded box may be any finite non-negative real, is not forced to 0, and is not subject to container boundary or support checks. For a loaded box, z+dz <= container_height. Each loaded box b with z>0 must have exactly one other loaded box a satisfying: z_a+dz_a=z_b, x_a<=x_b, x_b+dx_b<=x_a+dx_a, y_a<=y_b, y_b+dy_b<=y_a+dy_a; together these conditions define full direct support of b by a. No box may be left unsupported in mid-air, and no box may be supported by two or more boxes pieced together. A loaded box with z=0 is supported by the floor and needs no other box underneath; one supporting box may carry multiple boxes, each fully supported by it and satisfying all other constraints.

decisions.business: Orientation number of candidate box k of box type i. 0 when not loaded; when loaded it may only be 1, 2, or 3, meaning the original length, original width, or original height points vertically upward, respectively. For a loaded box, orientation 1 gives (dx,dy,dz)=(box_widths[i],box_heights[i],box_lengths[i]); orientation 2 gives (box_lengths[i],box_heights[i],box_widths[i]); orientation 3 gives (box_lengths[i],box_widths[i],box_heights[i]). dx, dy, dz lie along the spatial x, y, z axes respectively; additionally swapping the two horizontal edges or any other rotation is not allowed.
decisions.shape: list[list[int]]; outer length exactly N, row i has length exactly box_quantities[i]; the first array axis is box type i and the second is candidate box k, both 0-based; elements are only the integers 0, 1, 2, 3, booleans not accepted. [] when N=0, and rows for zero-quantity box types must be [].
decisions.completeness: An orientation entry must be given for every candidate box; do not omit it or use null. When s[i][k]=0, o[i][k] must be 0; when s[i][k]=1, o[i][k] must be in {1,2,3} and orientation_allowed[i][o[i][k]-1]=1. For each loaded box b, following the full direct support relation defined in the z field, all boxes reachable upward from b directly or indirectly form its set of descendants above; this set covers all levels and all branches. The sum of the descendants' self-weights box_weights[their box type] (each descendant counted once, excluding b itself) must be <= dx_b×dy_b×load_bearing_by_orientation[box_type_b][o_b-1]; do not count only the immediately upper layer, and do not treat the per-area load-bearing component directly as the total load capacity. With no descendants the load is 0; boxes on the floor must also satisfy this limit; there is no separate floor load-bearing limit. Under an orientation with zero load-bearing, there must be no boxes above transmitting positive weight to that box. Unloaded boxes do not participate in support relations or load-bearing computation.
